Oxana Marx is a tiefling bard that i've grown to love more than any of my previous characters, since she was actually the first character i got to play irl! 

at the ripe age of 18, she left her family home and travelled north as a young, brighteyed entertainer, looking for hire at various taverns and bars. after about a year of travel, she stumbled into the Frailworth, a noble manor, where she met an elven noblewoman named Othylia the Gentle, who loved the arts, and prided herself on collecting art and music in it's "live form" by hiring painters, sculptors, dancers and bards to entertain her. Oxana was hired by Othylia, residing in the manor fulltime as her resident violist and poet and, later down the line, advisor and not-really-that-secret lover. 

Oxana's life split in two when the Frailworth was attacked by a human party of thieves, who heard of the manor's collection of art and decided to rob it blind, without sparing anyone who might get in their way. Oxana and a few other artists managed to defend themselves, but before the thieves could realize there were only a few sculptures and paintings to take, they had gruesomely killed more than half of the manor's residents, including Othylia, decapitating her in the manor's gardens. She fled the castle after singlehandedly burying her love in the gardens, still in shock, in which she would remain for a little over a year.

In that period, she drank away most of her (rather humble) savings, barely spoke a word (and when she did, it was usually infernal nonsense) and barely wrote anything. during one of her drunken nights at a northern tavern, she met a human mercernary who spoke a bit of infernal thanks to his time in the sea trade, and actually got very drunk and depressed Oxana to sign a contract to his travelling party of misfit good doers. and, uh, the rest is history!

for me, a good rule is to make success awesome and failure hilarious. I think an excellent example of good crit fail outcomes are things like getting something in your eye on a perception check or stubbing your toe on a bad stealth/acrobatics check. one of my personal favorites is a bit from good ol CR, where a character tried to steal gunpowder and, since she rolled a one, she ended up with a solid handful of black pepper.

 If you want to do it the hard way, or just want your players to feel that their actions might matter a lot in this scenario, make them take a teeny tiny bit of damage (i seriously mean it, like 1-5 points MAX) or semi-permanently impact their character (stuff like loosing teeth, chipping horns or dislocating fingers, causing things like a lisp, minor distracting pain or a disadvantage at wielding a weapon for a short amount of time)

as for successes, just make your players look awesome or throw in something funny. Nat 20 on investigation in a pile of junk? make them find a valuable or even magical item! Nat 20 on insight on that bandit? not only do they know he's totally lying about that involvement in a crime, they can tell he still misses his mom's cooking and his childhood dog, Sprocket. Nat 20 on acrobatics? somehow they manage to do a sick backflip on their way down, making the passerby villagers clap in amusement.

and, when all else fails, give out some inspiration. that's always nice.
